look_here_first: Start with flower color. White rosinweed is the standout Silphium in this project because its ray florets are white, while the nearby Silphium comparisons have yellow heads. Then confirm the tough rough/scabrous foliage, often deeply divided, on dry limestone or calcareous prairie.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves often deeply pinnately lobed or divided

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dry limestone/calcareous prairie and open slopes

lookalikes.differences: White rays are the fastest split from nearby Silphium. S. laciniatum can also have deeply divided leaves but has yellow heads; S. radula has broad rough sessile leaves and yellow heads; S. integrifolium has broad entire leaves and yellow heads.
